items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses John Coltrane's musical style and history ('Trane was searching for something... played with everybody') but does not describe a direct personal or professional interaction with him. The interviewee mentions being in the same venue (Birdland) as Coltrane's band ('opposite t

ctx.x: -- in turmoil and the revolutionaries were talking about John Coltrane, his book of poetry. If you collected all the things that were written in the '60s on Trane, you could have a nice anthology just on him from the poetry.

Well, Trane was searching for something. Trane -- musically, Trane played everything. He had played it all, played with everybody. So he was searching for another sound, another way of getting over his horn, you know? At times, he was booed by people that, you know, wanted to hear some of that, what they call his best moments supposedly, the part where he was playing so-called "Sheets of Sound,"
you know, he took it further than that.
